Liam Park: Hey all, first week question 1 — installed Okta Gateway on Windows and cant SSH to private bastion (10.3.4.5). Windows shows connected but SSH times out from WSL2. Anyone seen this?
Devon Ng: welcome Liam! yep WSL2 often doesn't inherit Windows VPN routes/DNS. Quick steps: 1) re-auth Okta in browser (forces route/DNS push), 2) if still broken, either add route inside WSL (`sudo ip route add 10.3.0.0/16 via <WSL_GW>`) or add hosts entry on Windows and `wsl --shutdown` to pick it up. Which did you try?
Liam Park: I re-authed Okta (okta-bot asked for MFA) but WSL still couldn't resolve `bastion.corp`. `ip route` in WSL has no 10.3/16 route.
Devon Ng: try `wsl --shutdown` then restart WSL. If that fails, temporary inside WSL: `sudo ip route add 10.3.0.0/16 via 172.28.16.1` (use your default gw). Also DNS: WSL regenerates /etc/resolv.conf, so to persist corp DNS you can disable auto-gen with `/etc/wsl.conf` and write resolv.conf manually.
Liam Park: added the route inside WSL and ssh to 10.3.4.5 worked! Thanks. FYI my SSH key still needed to be uploaded to my profile for key-based auth.
infra-bot: Liam Park's IAM tag `corp-ssh-access` is pending approval. Infra team: please review to enable SSM console sessions.
Liam Park: oh noted, I filed the infra request in #eng-infra with my employee ID.
Devon Ng: we'll add a note to the new-hire Windows checklist: "After Okta Gateway install, re-auth in browser, then `wsl --shutdown` to sync routes/DNS; fallback: add WSL route or persist resolv.conf." Saves folks a bunch of headache.
okta-bot: Okta Gateway session refreshed for Liam Park. MFA confirmed.
Liam Park: all set now, thanks everyone! tagging this thread for future new-hires: re-auth Okta + sync routes to WSL (or add WSL route) + ensure ssh key uploaded. :tada:
